abstracts.abstract: This paper proposes a novel unified theoretical framework for intelligent systems called Hierarchical Cognitive Architecture (HCA), which fundamentally reconceptualizes the integration of symbolic reasoning and connectionist learning. Traditional approaches to artificial intelligence have treated fuzzy logic, neural networks, and genetic algorithms as separate paradigms requiring ad-hoc integration strategies. The proposed HCA framework establishes formal mathematical foundations for knowledge representation across multiple abstraction levels, enabling seamless transition between symbolic and sub-symbolic processing. We introduce the concept of cognitive momentum, which captures the dynamic evolution of system understanding through iterative refinement cycles. The theoretical analysis demonstrates that HCA satisfies fundamental completeness conditions for universal intelligent system design, establishing convergence properties for hybrid learning architectures. Mathematical proofs are provided establishing the equivalence between HCA states and standard fuzzy cognitive map configurations under specific boundary conditions. The framework's theoretical implications extend to knowledge engineering by providing normative guidelines for expert system development that transcend current paradigm limitations. Experimental validation on benchmark pattern recognition tasks confirms the theoretical predictions regarding computational complexity reduction. This paradigm innovation offers a foundational shift in how intelligent agents construct, maintain, and retrieve domain knowledge, potentially influencing future developments in cognitive systems research.

This paper presents a significant theoretical advancement in fuzzy cognitive map theory by introducing time-weighted adaptive learning mechanisms that substantially improve prediction accuracy in dynamic decision support scenarios. Conventional fuzzy cognitive maps suffer from static weight assignment, which limits their effectiveness in non-stationary environments requiring continuous knowledge adaptation. The proposed Temporal Weighted Fuzzy Cognitive Maps (TW-FCM) extend traditional formulations through novel temporal decay functions that modulate causal relationship strengths based on recency and relevance factors. We develop comprehensive learning algorithms that combine gradient descent optimization with genetic algorithm-inspired population-based search, enabling simultaneous weight refinement and structure optimization. The theoretical analysis establishes convergence bounds for the proposed hybrid learning approach, demonstrating quadratic convergence rates under mild regularity conditions. Furthermore, we prove that TW-FCM subsumes standard fuzzy cognitive maps as a special case when temporal parameters are set to uniform values. Extensive simulation studies across multiple application domains—including financial forecasting, medical diagnosis, and intelligent control—demonstrate consistent performance improvements of 15-30% over baseline approaches. The theoretical framework also provides guidelines for parameter initialization that accelerate learning convergence. This advancement extends the practical applicability of knowledge-based fuzzy systems in real-world intelligent system deployments requiring adaptive decision support capabilities.

This paper presents NeuroCogX, a novel cognitive architecture for intelligent agents that fundamentally reimagines the integration of neural network learning with symbolic reasoning through a hierarchical memory-augmented design. Unlike existing cognitive systems that treat perception, cognition, and action as loosely coupled modules, NeuroCogX establishes tight integration through three novel architectural components: the Semantic Binding Layer, the Episodic Compression Network, and the Goal-State Projection Engine. The Semantic Binding Layer enables dynamic formation of symbolic representations from distributed neural activations, supporting flexible knowledge engineering without manual rule specification. The Episodic Compression Network implements intelligent control mechanisms that prioritize and consolidate experiences based on predictive utility, mimicking biological consolidation processes observed in cognitive systems. The Goal-State Projection Engine provides intelligent decision support through counterfactual reasoning capabilities that were previously absent in neural architecture designs. System implementation demonstrates successful operation across diverse task domains including autonomous navigation, resource optimization, and collaborative problem-solving. The architecture supports real-time learning without catastrophic forgetting through novel replay mechanisms that preserve representational geometry. Performance evaluations against state-of-the-art cognitive architectures reveal substantial improvements in sample efficiency and transfer learning capabilities. The proposed design paradigm establishes new directions for constructing intelligent agents capable of lifelong learning and adaptive behavior in complex, dynamic environments.

This paper presents an enhanced expert system architecture for medical decision support that significantly improves diagnostic accuracy through a hybrid approach integrating deep neural networks with knowledge-based reasoning mechanisms. Traditional expert systems rely exclusively on rule-based inference derived from knowledge engineering efforts, limiting their ability to handle cases exhibiting subtle pattern recognition requirements. Conversely, pure machine learning approaches lack the interpretability and causal reasoning capabilities essential for clinical deployment. The proposed MedExpert+ system addresses these limitations through three key innovations: a symptom-guided attention mechanism that directs neural feature extraction toward clinically relevant regions, a knowledge graph integration module enabling causal reasoning over disease relationships, and an uncertainty quantification framework providing calibrated confidence estimates for all diagnostic outputs. System evaluation employs a comprehensive dataset comprising 180,000 patient records across 847 distinct conditions, demonstrating 12.4% improvement in top-5 diagnostic accuracy compared to previous expert system implementations. Interpretability analysis confirms that the knowledge graph integration successfully constrains neural predictions to clinically plausible hypotheses. The uncertainty quantification module achieves calibration error below 0.03, satisfying clinical deployment requirements. Integration with existing hospital information systems is achieved through standardized APIs, enabling practical deployment. This system design advances the state-of-the-art in intelligent decision support for healthcare applications, balancing the accuracy benefits of machine learning with the explainability demands of medical practice.
